hero.filename: Canine Distemper Virus Cytoplasmic Inclusion Body (Blood smear, Wright's stain).jpg
hero.caption: Canine Distemper virus cytoplasmic inclusion body within a neutrophil (blood smear, Wright's Stain). This was found on the blood smear of a 1-month-old, female, mixed breed puppy that presented with signs consistent with upper respiratory disease and conjunctivitis.  Diagnostics revealed that the dog had leukocytosis (23,200 WBCs/ul), anemia (PCV 22.2%), and hypoproteinemia (total protein 5.4 g/dl).

images.caption: Old cemetery, Bonn, North Rhine-Westphalia, GermanyThe Old Cemetery in Bonn, laid out in 1715 under Elector Joseph Clemens, is now one of the most important cemeteries in Germany. Originally designed as a burial place for soldiers and the poor outside the city walls, in the 19th century it became the preferred resting place for the upper middle classes and professors at the University of Bonn.The area is a unique reflection of cultural epochs from Baroque to Classicism to Historicism. Famous personalities such as Robert and Clara Schumann, Beethoven’s mother Maria Magdalena Keverich, and Ernst Moritz Arndt found their final resting place here. The magnificent Schumann tomb by Adolf von Donndorf is particularly worth seeing. Since the cemetery was closed for general burials in 1884, its historical appearance as a “stone chronicle” has been largely preserved. Today, the site serves as a memorial and park, maintained by the city of Bonn and the Alter Friedhof Community Foundation.
